title: A finite public matrix family with relative Frobenius approximation.
summary: Minimize $\|A-B\|_{\mathrm{F}}$ over the finite public matrix family $\mathcal{F}$.

task.description_zh: Minimize $\|A-B\|_{\mathrm F}$ over the finite public matrix family $\mathcal F$.
description_paragraphs: Minimize $\|A-B\|_{\mathrm{F}}$ over the finite public matrix family $\mathcal{F}$.

model.description_zh: The object $A\in\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is arbitrary; $\mathcal F\subset\mathbb R^{d\times d}$ is finite and nonempty, and $|\mathcal F|=M$ holds. The condition $A\in\mathcal F$ is not required. The relative factor is $\gamma\ge1$.

guarantees.description_zh: The algorithm is selected using public inputs only. For every admissible input fixed before generation of the private seed, success probability over private randomness is at least $1-\delta$.
guarantees.complete_expression: Choose one algorithm, then require success probability at least $1-\delta$ on every fixed admissible input, over the algorithm’s private randomness. The input is independent of the private seed. Average correctness under an input distribution is insufficient.
guarantees.quantifier_order: exists algorithm or specified procedure; for every fixed legal input and every allowed feedback rule; then probability over private seed where present

domains.definition: Return $\widehat B\in\mathcal F$. If represented by a candidate index, it must uniquely identify the matrix. No error certificate is required.

norms.definition: Euclidean vector norm $\|z\|_2=(\sum_i|z_i|^2)^{1/2}$ and matrix operator norm $\|M\|_{\rm op}=\max_{\|z\|_2=1}\|Mz\|_2$; define $\|M\|_F=(\sum_{ij}|M_{ij}|^2)^{1/2}$.

comparators.definition: Minimize $\|A-B\|_{\mathrm F}$ over the finite public matrix family $\mathcal F$. Define $\operatorname{OPT}=\min_{B\in\mathcal F}\|A-B\|_{\mathrm F}$; success requires $\|A-\widehat B\|_{\mathrm F}\le\gamma\operatorname{OPT}$. A zero optimum requires exact recovery.

proofs.title: Deterministic standard-basis reconstruction and candidate enumeration
proofs.body: Recover the $d$ columns by standard basis queries. Evaluate every public candidate's Frobenius residual internally and choose an exact minimizer, with a fixed public tie rule. This attains the family optimum and therefore satisfies every allowed multiplicative factor at least one, including zero optimal residual.
proofs.scope: All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

evidence.supports: QSL Theorem 1 obtains a (3 + η)-factor Frobenius residual guarantee for any fully public finite matrix family using products with the matrix and its transpose. Set η = γ − 3. Candidate search and public-matrix arithmetic do not count as oracle queries.
notes: QSL Theorem 1 obtains a (3 + η)-factor Frobenius residual guarantee for any fully public finite matrix family using products with the matrix and its transpose. Set η = γ − 3. Candidate search and public-matrix arithmetic do not count as oracle queries.

evidence.supports: Some public finite family requires Omega(sqrt(log M/log gamma)) general randomized adaptive two-sided queries. Its size and dimension are coupled by the source's covering-net construction.
notes: The query lower bound also takes the worst case over the public family F. It does not imply that each fixed F requires this many queries. Exact endpoint realization for every prescribed integer M has not been established.
